name: Sint Maarten

findings.summary: Nokia Siemens Networks won a turnkey contract to supply TelCell, the mobile arm of state-owned TelEm Group, with a 3G/HSPA network covering Flexi Multiradio base stations and core elements (MSC server, gateway nodes, NetAct management).
findings.analyst_inference: NSN was a Finnish-German joint venture, now wholly Nokia (Finland), so pole third. Both trade-press items probably derive from the same vendor release, so independence is weak. Coded at tier 3 (contract); launch was only expected end-April 2011 and not confirmed. Pre-2020 and no evidence on whether TelCell's later LTE layer still uses Nokia, so still_current null.

findings.controller: NSW Submarine Cable Systems (a Corning Cable Systems company), turnkey supplier
findings.local_actor: SMITCOMS (St. Maarten international carrier); TelEm Group named as SMPR-1 owner in 2024
findings.builder: NSW Submarine Cable Systems (Corning Cable Systems)
findings.summary: SMITCOMS contracted Corning's NSW Submarine Cable Systems for a turnkey 374 km Puerto Rico to St. Maarten undersea cable. TelEm Group reported repairing its SMPR-1 cable off San Juan in August 2024 after an eight-year outage.
findings.analyst_inference: Vendor claim rests on Light Reading alone; the Daily Herald item confirms SMPR-1 exists and is TelEm-owned but names no vendor, so not treated as corroborating. Linking the 2003 SMITCOMS contract to the cable named SMPR-1 is an inference from route (Puerto Rico to St. Maarten). NSW was German-based but Corning (US) owned it at the time, so pole us; terminal equipment vendor unknown and any later upgrade unknown. Post-repair tests were pending, so still_current null.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Justice / St. Maarten Police Force (Camera Surveillance Centre); TelEm Group (connection and maintenance)
findings.summary: A government camera surveillance system, launched in Philipsburg in 2016 (phase one about NAf 2 million) with TelEm connection and maintenance, went live with a police-run monitoring centre in early 2019, billed as the start of a smart-city concept.
findings.analyst_inference: Neither article names the camera or software manufacturer, so the equipment controller and pole are unknown (null); the operator is domestic. Value converted from NAf 2,000,000 at the fixed peg of NAf 1.79 per USD (phase one only). Both sources are one outlet, so not corroborated. No AI analytics are documented.
